MoreSpace/Industries/Manufacturing/Buyer & order journey

Every stage, every handoff, every owner.

Follow the buyer & order journey from first contact to repeat relationship. Each stage shows its touchpoints, the accountable role, and the automations that support it. Each dot is one automation.

1

Enquiry & qualification

A buyer, OEM sourcing team or prospective dealer finds you on a B2B marketplace, your website, at a trade fair or through a rep, and sends an enquiry or RFQ. The same RFQ often goes to several suppliers, so a quick, informed first question matters.

Touchpoints

  • IndiaMART and TradeIndia enquiries
  • Website RFQ forms
  • Trade fair and exhibition leads
  • Calls and emails to sales
  • Dealer and distributor referrals

Accountable owner

Sales coordinator or inside sales lead

Automations on this stage

  • Enquiry & qualificationMarketplace and website enquiry capture with routingPull every enquiry from IndiaMART, TradeIndia, the website and the RFQ inbox into one CRM queue, remove duplicates, extract what the buyer needs and route it to the right product or territory owner with a response deadline.3–5 weeks
2

Specification, samples & quote

Engineering or R&D confirms what is needed, estimation builds the cost, and samples or trial lots may go to the buyer or brand client. Quotes pass technical and commercial review before release.

Touchpoints

  • Drawing and specification review
  • Costing and estimation
  • Samples and trial lots
  • Quotation and negotiation
  • Artwork and label approvals

Accountable owner

Estimation or applications engineering head

Automations on this stage

  • Specification, samples & quoteRFQ-to-quote drafting with estimator approvalTurn RFQ emails, drawings and BOQs into a structured costing draft based on your item master, past quotes and current rates, so the estimator reviews and approves a quote instead of building it from scratch, and the eventual PO is checked against it.6–10 weeks
  • Specification, samples & quotePrivate-label sample, artwork and approval trackingTrack each brand client's brief, samples, feedback rounds, artwork and label approvals and first-order readiness in one shared portal, so both sides can see what is pending and who must act next.5–7 weeks
3

Order & credit check

A purchase order or dealer order arrives and is checked against the quote or price list, schemes, stock and credit before a sales order is created in the ERP and acknowledged.

Touchpoints

  • Customer purchase orders
  • Dealer orders on WhatsApp, calls or a portal
  • Price list and scheme checks
  • Stock and credit limit checks
  • Order acknowledgement

Accountable owner

Sales operations or order desk manager

Automations on this stage

  • Order & credit checkDealer and distributor ordering on WhatsApp or a portalLet registered dealers place orders on WhatsApp or a simple portal, validated against the ERP price list, schemes, pack sizes, stock and credit position before a draft sales order reaches the order desk.4–6 weeks
4

Plan, procure, make & check

Planning schedules production, purchase secures materials, the shop floor produces, maintenance keeps equipment running, and quality inspects, records non-conformances and releases batches.

Touchpoints

  • Production planning
  • Supplier POs and material receipts
  • Shift production and downtime
  • Inspection, NCR and CAPA
  • Preventive maintenance
  • QC testing and batch release

Accountable owner

Plant head

Automations on this stage

  • Plan, procure, make & checkDaily production and OEE-style reporting from ERP and MES dataCollect shift production, downtime and rejection entries from the ERP, MES or shift sheets, check them for gaps, and publish a plant dashboard and a short written summary in time for the morning production meeting.4–6 weeks
  • Plan, procure, make & checkQuality NCR, customer complaint and CAPA routingRaise non-conformances and customer complaints with photos, lot and part details, route them to the right quality owner, track containment and CAPA actions to closure, and draft 8D reports for QA approval.4–6 weeks
  • Plan, procure, make & checkPreventive maintenance alerts and breakdown loggingGenerate maintenance work orders from calendar, run-hour or count schedules, remind technicians and supervisors before due dates, log breakdowns with cause and spares used, and track statutory inspection dates.4–6 weeks
  • Plan, procure, make & checkSupplier PO follow-ups and inbound material trackingFollow up open purchase orders before their due dates, read supplier replies into expected dates for the buyer to confirm, and flag shortages against the production plan or dealer backorders.2–4 weeks
  • Plan, procure, make & checkBatch release readiness tracker around validated systemsShow, for every batch, whether production records, QC tests, deviations and documents are complete by reading status from validated systems, and remind the right reviewers, without touching the GxP record itself.5–8 weeks
5

Invoice, dispatch & deliver

Goods are packed and invoiced with an e-invoice IRN where applicable, moved under an e-way bill, handed to a transporter or CHA, and delivered with the documents the buyer needs.

Touchpoints

  • E-invoice and e-way bill
  • Transporter and vehicle assignment
  • CoA, safety data sheets and test certificates
  • Export documents and CHA
  • Proof of delivery

Accountable owner

Logistics and dispatch lead

Automations on this stage

  • Invoice, dispatch & deliverDispatch updates with invoice, e-way bill and documentsWhen an order is invoiced and dispatched, send the buyer the invoice, e-way bill number, transporter and vehicle details, plus the CoA and safety data sheet where needed, and alert the dispatch team before an e-way bill expires in transit.3–5 weeks
  • Invoice, dispatch & deliverExport documentation checklist for chemical and pharma shipmentsFor each export order, build the document checklist by destination, incoterm and product, prefill drafts from ERP data, check consistency across documents and track every item through to the shipping bill and bill of lading.4–6 weeks
6

Payment & collections

Invoices fall due under agreed terms. Accounts reconciles receipts, credit notes and disputes, and follows up overdue balances, which in turn decide whether the next order can be released.

Touchpoints

  • Ledger statements
  • Payment reminders
  • Credit notes and scheme claims
  • Short-supply and quality disputes
  • Credit holds and releases

Accountable owner

Credit controller or accounts receivable lead

Automations on this stage

  • Payment & collectionsCredit-limit checks and overdue payment remindersCompute each dealer's exposure against their credit limit every day, flag orders for hold, and send courteous ledger-based reminders before and after due dates, with escalation to the rep and then the credit controller.3–5 weeks
7

Service, field visits & reorder

After delivery, customers need installation, AMC visits, warranty support and spares, while reps visit dealers to secure reorders and resolve issues. How this stage goes often decides the next order.

Touchpoints

  • Installation and commissioning
  • Warranty and AMC service
  • Spare-part requests
  • Rep visits to dealers and retailers
  • Repeat orders

Accountable owner

Service manager and regional sales manager

Automations on this stage

  • Service, field visits & reorderService, AMC and warranty tickets with spare-part requestsLog service requests with machine serial number, photos and symptoms, check warranty or AMC status, assign the right engineer, suggest checks from approved manuals and turn spare-part needs into stock checks or quotes.6–8 weeks
  • Service, field visits & reorderSales rep beat planning and visit reportingPlan weekly dealer and retailer beats from sales, overdue and stock data, then let reps report each visit as a short WhatsApp voice note or form that becomes a structured CRM record and a daily summary for managers.4–6 weeks

Where people stay in control

Automation handles the predictable steps. These are the decisions that stay with an accountable person.

AutomationStageHuman checkpoint
Marketplace and website enquiry capture with routingEnquiry & qualificationThe sales coordinator reviews low-confidence extractions, out-of-territory enquiries and anything flagged as a large or strategic account before routing. Reps qualify every enquiry by call or email; the automation never sends prices or delivery commitments.
RFQ-to-quote drafting with estimator approvalSpecification, samples & quoteThe estimator or applications engineer checks every technical interpretation, cost element and price before release, and the sales head approves discounts outside the matrix. Nothing reaches a buyer without a named approver recorded against that quote version.
Dealer and distributor ordering on WhatsApp or a portalOrder & credit checkThe order desk releases every order with an exception: unclear SKUs, price or scheme overrides, stock shortfalls or credit flags. Orders on credit hold are released only by the credit controller. Prices and schemes always come from the ERP, never from the AI.
Credit-limit checks and overdue payment remindersPayment & collectionsThe credit controller decides credit limits, holds, releases, extensions and any legal step. Reminders use approved, non-threatening wording, and an open dispute pauses reminders for that invoice until a person resolves it.
Dispatch updates with invoice, e-way bill and documentsInvoice, dispatch & deliverThe dispatch lead handles every exception; vehicle changes and e-way bill extensions are made in the e-way bill system by the dispatch team or the transporter carrying the goods. The automation never generates, cancels or extends e-invoices or e-way bills; it reads status and alerts people. Only QC releases CoAs.
Sales rep beat planning and visit reportingService, field visits & reorderArea managers approve beat plans and review exceptions. Reps confirm each extracted visit record before it is saved. The system reports planned and completed visits only; any decision about a rep's performance rests with their manager, using fuller context.
Service, AMC and warranty tickets with spare-part requestsService, field visits & reorderThe service engineer diagnoses and decides the repair, and the service manager approves warranty acceptance or rejection and any goodwill. Faults involving guarding, interlocks, pressure or electrical hazards go straight to an engineer; the assistant never advises bypassing a safety device.
Daily production and OEE-style reporting from ERP and MES dataPlan, procure, make & checkLine supervisors confirm reason codes and corrections before figures are published, and the plant head reviews the written summary and owns any action. For GxP plants the dashboard is a reporting copy; batch records in validated systems remain the record.
Quality NCR, customer complaint and CAPA routingPlan, procure, make & checkThe QA manager decides disposition (use as is, rework, scrap or return) and approves root cause, CAPA closure and every customer-facing report. AI output is marked as draft and never closes a record. On GxP sites, deviations and CAPAs stay in the validated QMS.
Preventive maintenance alerts and breakdown loggingPlan, procure, make & checkThe maintenance head approves schedule changes and every deferral, and safety-critical tasks cannot be deferred without a named sign-off. For GxP equipment, calibration and maintenance records stay in the validated CMMS or logbook; this workflow only sends reminders.
Supplier PO follow-ups and inbound material trackingPlan, procure, make & checkThe buyer confirms every revised date before it reaches planning. Changes to PO price, quantity or supplier are made only by the purchase manager in the ERP. Shortfalls of client-supplied material are raised with the brand client by the account manager.
Export documentation checklist for chemical and pharma shipmentsInvoice, dispatch & deliverThe export documentation executive verifies every document before release. HS and dangerous goods classification and regulatory documents are decided by the trade compliance or regulatory owner, and the CHA files the shipping bill. The automation never submits a filing.
Private-label sample, artwork and approval trackingSpecification, samples & quoteR&D or QA releases each sample. The manufacturer's regulatory or QA owner confirms label declarations for the product category, such as Legal Metrology, FSSAI, cosmetics or drug labeling rules. The brand client's named approver signs off artwork in the portal before printing.
Batch release readiness tracker around validated systemsPlan, procure, make & checkOnly QA releases or rejects a batch, following site SOPs in the validated systems. The tracker is a read-only, non-GxP reporting layer introduced through the site's change control, and it never creates, edits or approves a GxP record or signature.
